rows.answer:
The heaters ran on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours before launch to empty the tank [1]. The Review Board traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 [2]. The cause was its thermostatic switches, which were built for 28 volts and were not changed when the heater specification moved to 65 volts in 1965 [3][4]. North American Aviation made that heater revision [5], and Beech Aircraft, which built the tank's switches, did not change them [6]. The board called that switch failure a serious oversight that all parties share [7].
